$schema.note: One record per district, keyed STATE-NN, holding ONLY the fields the state election article cannot supply. Merged over data/house-2026.json at render time by race-data.js.
$schema.rule: NEVER write a value you have not read on the cited source. Omit a field or leave it null rather than recalling it — null and empty arrays are skipped by the merge, so a partial record is safe.
$schema.fields: pres24 {name, party, margin, newLines, shift, shiftParty} · counties [string] · tenure {type: incumbent|party|flipped, name, party, since} · history [{year, name, party, margin}] · redistricted (bool) · house24 {dPct, rPct, margin} to add the vote split · sources {bpRace, bpCandidates} · checked
$schema.priority: history and tenure are worth pulling only for competitive districts (any tilt/lean/toss-up rating). pres24 and counties come from all-district tables, not per-district pages.
$schema.pres20: Same shape as pres24, from the same Downballot file. Captured but not rendered — reserved for a trend line.
$schema.presSource: "downballot" = The Downballot's 2020 & 2024 presidential results for the districts used in the 2026 elections (Singer, Donner, Nir; the-db.co/presbycd). Computed on CURRENT lines, so newLines is intentionally unset: the card reads "2024 PRESIDENT / District-level result" rather than claiming a recompute the source does not frame that way.
$schema.counties: Every county the district touches, alphabetical, '(part)' where the district covers only part of it. From the Census Bureau's 119th-Congress CD-to-county relationship file, so it is written ONLY for the 40 states whose lines are unchanged for 2026 — the ten redistricted states have no published 2026 county file and are left empty rather than described wrongly. Ordering is alphabetical on purpose: the source carries land area, not population, so any 'largest first' order would imply an importance it cannot support.
$schema.history: Winner, party and margin for the last five cycles from the MIT Election Data and Science Lab's U.S. House 1976-2024 returns. Rows before 2022 carry oldLines:true — every state redrew after the 2020 census, so those margins describe a differently shaped district.
$schema.tenure: Earliest year of the incumbent's UNBROKEN run of wins in this district, walked across the FULL MIT returns (1976-2024) so a long-tenured member is never reported at the window floor. 'elected' is the election year; 'since' is the January they took office, which is what the page prints. The run breaks where the district number changes hands, so a member who held a differently numbered seat earlier reads from the year this seat's run began — not a career first-elected year.
$schema.redistricted: true only where the state's own article states a new map is in effect for 2026 (ten states). redistrictNote quotes what the article says. This flips the 2024 House card to 'OLD LINES', which is correct there and wrong everywhere else.
$schema.house24: From the state article (the incumbent's own 2024 share). For unchanged districts the MIT returns add dPct/rPct/margin so the card can show the real D-R split.
